description: Main window: core defaults; open/save dialogs and the plugin's message dialog ("... already exists. Replace it?": the plugin replaces window.confirm with an asynchronous one that needs it; the question over unsaved changes is the page's own dialog since #120 and needs no permission); reading and writing files, limited to the paths the user picked in a dialog or dropped on the window (lane 6). The app's own commands (device_public_key, device_sign, open_external) are allowed by default; the opener plugin is driven from Rust, so no opener, shell or http permission is granted to the webview (lane 8). Plugins (lane 11): reading and writing under $APPDATA (installed plugins live in $APPDATA/plugins) and listing folders the user picked in a dialog (Load unpacked folder). Closing over unsaved changes (lane 35): the page hears the shell's sawhorse://close-requested event (core:default's event listening), asks with its own dialog, and answers through the app's own close_guard command, which also carries File > Exit and, while a save chosen at the question runs, the word "saving"; the shell closes or destroys the window itself, so no core:window permission (close, destroy) is granted to the webview. The file the app was started with (lane 37): the app's own start_file command, allowed by default, hands its path over once and adds exactly that path to the fs scope, so the page reads it through the fs plugin with the permissions a dropped file is read with; no permission is added. The window's title (lane 39): the page sends the text of its own title to the app's own window_title command, allowed by default, which cleans it and sets it on the calling window only; no core:window permission (set-title) is granted to the webview. The Help menu (lane 67): the same open_external command opens the user guide, the changelog and the source on GitHub, exactly the three addresses in sawhorse_device_key::HELP_URLS, in the system browser; no permission is added. The folder a dialog starts in (#71, #80): the page names folders to the app's own dialog_folder command, allowed by default, which answers on Linux with the first of them, then Documents, then home, that is a folder the user can list now; it opens each to see that and reads no entry, writes nothing and adds nothing to the fs scope; no permission is added.
